findings.claim: The administrative-ledger append protocol has no durable post-invocation outcome even though its own contract requires the append receipt to bind actual success or failure and after-ledger hashes: the candidate and both RootControlJournal records are finalized before the ledger invocation, and the later APPLIED/NOT_APPLIED observation is not persisted.
findings.evidence_excerpt: “its operation receipt binds the activity invocation, before/after ledger hashes and actual success/failure” / “On observation, current==candidate is APPLIED; current==source is NOT_APPLIED and blocks rather than retrying.”
findings.impact: A failed, source-equal, timed-out, or unknown append cannot satisfy deterministic invocation/effect reconciliation. The control plane must either remain blocked permanently or infer post-effect evidence that was never immutably recorded, defeating the claimed fail-closed accounting basis for bootstrap, migration, admission, and recovery.
findings.recommended_action: Add a create-once post-invocation AdministrativeAppendAttemptOutcome in RootControlJournal that binds the authorization and candidate-commit IDs, observed current hash/version, APPLIED/NOT_APPLIED/UNKNOWN result, actual units, and observation receipt; require it before recovery and P15/P14 closure, with a missing outcome remaining fail-stop.

findings.claim: The AdministrativeResourceLedger does not define deterministic arithmetic between the full no-refund AdmissionResourceReservation debit and the later per-operation actual-usage entries, so the required cumulative usage and remaining-ceiling values can either double-count the same work or omit actual use from the global ceiling.
findings.evidence_excerpt: “cumulative usage; remaining ceiling” / “The append deducts the full reservation from globally available cumulative ceiling ... Each non-mutating operation appends its actual-usage entry”
findings.impact: Different conforming implementations can report incompatible remaining budget. Double counting can deadlock valid recovery, while treating actual entries as additional but non-debiting observations without an explicit reservation sub-balance can hide overrun and allow charge with insufficient contingency.
findings.recommended_action: Specify exact fields and equations for global committed units, reservation debit, reservation actual use, reservation remaining, append overhead, and global remaining ceiling. State explicitly that a unit is charged globally exactly once and require fixtures for full use, partial use, failure/UNKNOWN, exhaustion, and concurrent reservation rejection.

findings.claim: The migration protocol never defines an ordered successful commit that version-guard writes the accepted candidate to the canonical ledger and then re-reads, hash-checks, and strict-validates the persisted bytes before entering FROZEN(new base); step 7 says write before candidate validation, while the exit criterion binds only HUMAN acceptance of the candidate hash.
findings.evidence_excerpt: “7. Write a small current projection separately from immutable historical evidence when the contract permits it” / “8. Run strict validator ... on the exact candidate bytes.”
findings.impact: The procedure is ambiguous between validating an unpersisted staging candidate and mutating the canonical ledger before validation. It can declare migration complete without evidence that canonical bytes equal the HUMAN-accepted strict-valid base, causing an invalid unfreeze/WBS handoff or a later P3 deadlock.
findings.recommended_action: Define one explicit sequence: build a staged candidate, validate/review it, obtain HUMAN selection, authorize and perform one version-guarded canonical write from the pinned source, re-read and verify raw equality plus strict validation, independently verify the persisted bytes, and only then record final HUMAN byte acceptance and enter FROZEN(new base); route every failure through the bound restore path.
